spec_match.rationale: The page's central claim — that the (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) comma branch is a 'media-style condition' a single @container rule can fire on — is wrong per css-contain/css-conditional-5: inside @container it is an unknown query that parses but can never match, so the demo teaches a misconception.

interactive.rationale: The Read rule.conditionText button makes a real CSSOM call, but the other two buttons only hide/show fixed frames; nothing lets the user actually change a container width or fire the second branch (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card matches what the page attempts (size branch + 'user-preference query' + conditionText readback), but both repeat the incorrect user-preference framing against the spec.

edge_cases.rationale: In a pre-150 browser the comma rule fails to parse, so the 540/720 frames render tiles with a completely blank verdict and no capability notice; and the '360px (trigger)' frame never triggers because border-box padding shrinks the container below 360px.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/6196591858941952 and the CSS Conditional 5 container-rule section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts real parse/CSSOM/round-trip/unknown-branch contracts and fails honestly in this browser (1 pass / 4 fail / 0 blocked) — it genuinely distinguishes supporting browsers.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): fallback 'no match · cramped' verdicts render on 220/280/360, 540/720 verdicts are blank, frame bodies overflow their cards; buttons were not driven. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

telemetry_health.rationale: Baseline injected telemetry only; no page-level events for the CSSOM readback or match-state transitions.

design_system.rationale: Colours come from variables (including a color-mix of --accent-emerald), --font-display exists, and .ctl.on overrides background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: Controls are native buttons, but the show/hide toggles lack aria-pressed, match verdicts live in ::before pseudo-content with no live region, and the CSSOM output paragraph is not announced.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The fixed 540/720px frame bodies visibly overflow their card borders even at 1280px desktop, and at a 360px mobile viewport they guarantee unintended horizontal overflow with no scroll affordance.

openQuestions.title: Replace the prefers-reduced-motion branch — it can never match inside @container
openQuestions.detail: css-contain-3/css-conditional-5 container conditions evaluate size (and style()/scroll-state()) features; (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) is an unknown query inside @container, which the comma list tolerates but which always evaluates false. The demo's premise ('a single declaration handles both axes') is therefore false, and 'the rule' section explicitly mis-teaches it as media-style fall-through. Rebuild the second branch with something that can actually fire — e.g. style(--compact: on) or an orientation/aspect-ratio size branch — or repurpose the page to honestly demonstrate that unknown branches are tolerated-but-never-matching (which is what the suite's fallback-with-unknown-feature assertion proves).

openQuestions.title: Fix the 360px 'trigger' frame — it never triggers
openQuestions.detail: The frame-body carries width:360px plus padding and a 1px dashed border under the global border-box sizing, so the inline-size container measures ≈334px and (min-width: 360px) cannot match — the screenshot shows the trigger frame reading 'no match · cramped' even though the matrix labels it the trigger. Size the content box to a true 360px (or set the trigger at a width the content box actually reaches).

openQuestions.title: Add capability detection for pre-150 browsers instead of blank verdicts
openQuestions.detail: When the comma-separated rule fails to parse (Chromium ≤149), the 540/720 tiles show an empty verdict — a silent blank state. Feature-detect with CSS.supports on a comma list (the conformance suite's own probe) and show a 'requires Chrome 150+' notice, especially since the lineage note records the feature shipping in 150, not 149.

openQuestions.title: Contain the fixed-width frames on narrow viewports
openQuestions.detail: The 540/720px frame bodies overflow their cards on desktop and would force horizontal page overflow at ≈360px mobile. Wrap the matrix in an overflow-x:auto scroller (with a visible affordance) or scale the fixed widths down on narrow viewports while labelling the simulated width.

openQuestions.title: Announce state changes and mark toggle state
openQuestions.detail: Add aria-pressed to the Show-all/Hide toggles and aria-live=polite to #cssom-out so the conditionText readback and visibility changes are perceivable non-visually.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/comma-separated-container-queries/breakpoint-matrix/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 1 pass / 4 fail / 0 blocked — an honest suite that really distinguishes support). The screenshot alone exposes three real defects: the labelled 360px trigger frame reads 'no match · cramped' (border-box padding shrinks the container), the 540/720 frames show blank verdicts with no unsupported notice, and frame bodies overflow their cards. Deeper, the page's prefers-reduced-motion comma branch cannot ever match inside @container, so the demo's core teaching point contradicts the spec. Buttons and CSSOM readback were not driven headless.
